image_description: A tall, wooden bookcase with a classic design, featuring multiple shelves filled with books. The left section appears to have a glass door, while the right section is open shelving. The wood has a warm, reddish-brown finish. The bottom section includes cabinet doors or drawers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly a tall, vertical rectangular structure, consistent with standard bookcase proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Horizontal shelves are clearly visible dividing the vertical space into distinct sections.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bookcase is asymmetrical; the left side features a glazed/cabinet section while the right side is open shelving. It does not exhibit bilateral symmetry.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: At least 4-5 distinct shelf levels are visible in the right-hand section, spaced regularly.
Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature (pins/holes) that cannot be definitively verified from this external view/resolution.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left column of the bookcase shows reflections and framing consistent with a glass-fronted cabinet section.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual texture, grain pattern, and color variation strongly indicate stained wood construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The right-hand section is openly displaying numerous books spines-out.
The wood has a polished sheen, and small details suggesting handles or keyholes are faintly visible on the lower cabinet doors.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the book spines is illegible gibberish or non-existent patterns, typical of AI generation failing to render fine typography. Some spines appear to merge slightly.
The vertical line defining the left edge of the bookcase wavers and bleeds slightly into the background, lacking the crisp straightness expected of rigid furniture.
Minor inconsistencies in the perspective lines of the shelves; some appear to tilt slightly relative to others, though this could also be due to camera angle or old photography quality.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a bookcase and not a generic shelf or cabinet.
To verify the physical depth of the shelves and ensure books are sitting 'on' them rather than floating or merging.
To check for structural integrity of the frame and detect any melting edges or disconnected parts.
To assess the general sharpness and identify low-level noise or compression artifacts vs AI smearing.
To specifically analyze the legibility of text on book spines, a common failure point for AI generators.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of book spines
Straightness and parallelism of vertical/horizontal lines
Consistency of lighting and shadows within the shelf recesses
Boundary sharpness between the bookcase and the background
